newsitem.title: USA: Microchip backs Q3 revenue estimates.
newsitem.headline: Microchip backs Q3 revenue estimates.

text.p: Microchip Technology Inc, is comfortable with Wall Street estimates that its revenues will jump to $86 million in the quarter ending December, its chief financial officer said on Wednesday.
That would represent a 7.8 percent gain from the $79.5 million in revenue generated by Microchip in its fiscal second quarter ended in September.

CFO Phillip Chapman, speaking to an investor group at Montgomery Securities' technology conference, said Wall Street's average estimate of its third-quarter earnings was $0.41 a share. But he did not say whether Microchip was comfortable with that estimate.
Microchip posted second-quarter earnings of $0.37 a share. In the previous December quarter, it earned $0.16 a share.
Microchip, a maker of microcontroller chips embedded in everything from cellular telephones to car alarms, has put in place an aggressive schedule for introducing new products, Chapman said.
By the end of 1996, it will have introduced 40 products this year, he said. It introduced 21 products in 1995 and seven in 1994.
